# ACCESSORIES [italic]Lighters, cases and keepsakes, made by the House's own craftsmen or by a small number of houses it trusts.[/italic]
## LIGHTERS
- [bold]The Durbar[/bold], 120 pounds. A gold plated petrol lighter with the House seal engraved on the lid. Its click has been described as the most satisfying sound in the Empire. - [bold]The Envoy[/bold], 90 pounds. A slimmer lighter in polished steel, for diplomats who would prefer not to be seen with a gold one. - [bold]Balaji Matchbook[/bold], with every packet, free. Waxed matches, the House seal on the cover. The House prefers a match.
## CASES
- [bold]The Viceroy Case[/bold], 65 pounds. Holds a full packet out of its paper, for a man who does not want to be seen taking a cigarette from a packet. Fits an officer's breast pocket exactly, which the House measured.
## FOR THE TABLE
- [bold]The Malabar Ashtray[/bold], 40 pounds. Heavy glass, made in Firozabad, where glass has been made for longer than the Empire has existed. Too heavy to throw, which the House considers a feature.
## ENGRAVING Any lighter or case may be engraved at the Mumbai atelier with a name, a crest, a regiment or a date. The House will not engrave insults, Company logos or the names of former spouses.
